site.name: OpenAlt
site.tagline: The open source alternative to the tools you already pay for

tools.name: Notion
tools.summary: All-in-one workspace combining notes, documents, wikis and databases.

alternatives.why: The closest 1:1 replacement. Docs, databases and kanban boards in one offline-first app.
Docs and whiteboard on the same canvas. Stronger than Notion for visual thinking.
Outliner and personal knowledge base built on local Markdown files you own.
Block-based note taking with a built-in database and no subscription.

tools.name: Linear
tools.summary: Fast issue tracking built around keyboard-driven workflows.

alternatives.why: Cycles, modules and issues with a UI close enough that the switch takes an afternoon.
Full suite: issues, docs, HR and CRM in one self-hosted platform.
Lightweight task manager with lists, kanban and Gantt. Single binary.
Agile-first: epics, sprints and burndown charts. Older but battle-tested.

tools.name: Slack
tools.summary: Channel-based team messaging with integrations and huddles.

alternatives.why: The most mature Slack replacement. Channels, threads, playbooks and a large integration ecosystem.
Slack-style UI with omnichannel support: web, email and social in one inbox.
Threaded conversations that stay readable at scale. Best for async teams.
Matrix client. Federated, encrypted, and not owned by any single company.

tools.name: Figma
tools.summary: Browser-based interface design with real-time multiplayer editing.

alternatives.why: The only true Figma competitor: design and code in the same file, self-hostable.
Hand-drawn diagrams and wireframes. Much faster than Figma for early thinking.
Embeddable infinite canvas. A toolkit rather than a finished design app.
